title: consumption-safety-net-and-fastpath-onboarding-playbook-2026-09-01
author: Nadia Park
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook describes the Consumption Safety Net (CSN) and Fastpath Onboarding experience for new and migrating customers. It is a product-level guide that ties onboarding flows, runtime guardrails, telemetry, and pricing/credit reconciliation into a cohesive operation intended to reduce cost surprises while enabling rapid time-to-first-success.

Audience:
Product managers, onboarding engineers, solutions engineers, SRE, billing, and account teams.

Key goals:
- Provide a low-friction Fastpath onboarding route that exposes developers to a tuned default fidelity/cost profile.
- Implement a Safety Net that prevents runaway costs and preserves application availability through graceful fidelity degradation and crediting policies.
- Ensure telemetry and reconciliation primitives enable deterministic billing and customer-visible summaries.
- Define clear ownership, SLOs, rollout steps, and operational playbooks.

------------------------------------------------------------
Fastpath Onboarding (developer experience)

What Fastpath delivers:
1) Out-of-box configuration: a single predictable profile applied to an account on first project creation (named fastpath-default).
2) Developer-facing UX: Console quickstart with three toggles (Latency priority | Cost priority | Fidelity preview) and a short benchmark runner.
3) SDK/CLI preflight: automatic sample requests, token burn estimate, and safety-net checks before enabling production keys.

Fastpath default profile (applied to new projects):
- model: rwd-std-chat-1.0
- max_tokens_per_request: 512
- batch_window_ms: 30
- quantization_profile: q4_0_reduced_fp16
- prefix_cache: enabled (20MB per tenant)
- fallback_variant: rwd-mini-chat-0.9 (for burst or capacity failure)

Developer preflight checklist (in-console):
1. Run "Fastpath benchmark" (synthetic 20 requests)
2. Review estimated monthly unit cost given projected traffic
3. Confirm safety-net thresholds (default: monthly credit cap = $500 or 5x free credit)
4. Enable production keys or request Dedicated capacity via the Console bridge

CLI example (preflight):
$ redwood demo preflight --project my-app --profile fastpath-default
Expected output:
- median latency: 120ms
- tokens/req: 280
- estimated monthly cost @ 100k reqs/day: $2,100
- safety-net status: enabled (monthly cap: $500)

------------------------------------------------------------
Consumption Safety Net (CSN) - runtime guardrails

Concepts:
- Safety-net cap: a soft monetary cap associated with a project which surfaces to the Console and auto-limits traffic when hit.
- Graceful fidelity degradation: when cap or load events occur, system routes to lower-cost variants and reduces max_tokens_per_request incrementally.
- Fallback routing: automatic switch to fallback_variant for a project when primary variant latency or error rate exceeds SLA thresholds.

SLOs and thresholds (default for CSN):
- Monthly cap (soft): $500 (configurable per-tenant)
- Emergency throttle: 95th percentile token rate across a 5-minute window > 2x baseline -> start fidelity degradation
- Primary model latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for fastpath-default workloads
- Error budget: 0.5% request error rate per day before automated fallback

Guardrail actions (ordered):
1. Telemetry alert (Console + PagerDuty) when projected monthly spend reaches 75% of cap.
2. Send user notification and automatically reduce max_tokens_per_request by 20% (graceful degrade step 1).
3. If spend continues to rise and reaches 100% of cap, switch traffic to fallback_variant with preserved availability and notify billing/account team.
4. If fallback_variant saturated, apply rate limiting with header X-Redwood-Limit-Reached and return structured error suggesting purchase of additional capacity.

Config example (JSON) for project-level CSN toggles:
{
  "project_id": "proj_abc123",
  "consumption_safety_net": {
    "enabled": true,
    "monthly_cap_usd": 500,
    "degradation_steps": [
      "reduce_tokens_20pct",
      "switch_to_fallback",
      "apply_rate_limit"
    ]
  }
}

Note: The CSN config persists to the control plane and is enforced by the routing layer (redwood-router) and runtime (redwood-runtime).

------------------------------------------------------------
Telemetry and Reconciliation

Required telemetry events (names and minimal schema):
- csn.preflight.run -> {project_id, user_id, median_latency_ms, tokens_per_request, estimated_monthly_usd}
- csn.usage.sample -> {project_id, timestamp, tokens_consumed, model_variant}
- csn.degrade.event -> {project_id, step, reason, previous_config, new_config}
- csn.cap.hit -> {project_id, cap_usd, projected_monthly_usd}
- csn.fallback.switch -> {project_id, from_variant, to_variant, trigger_metric}

Reconciliation requirements:
- Billing-bridge must ingest csn.usage.sample on a 1m cadence into the billing pipeline.
- Discrepancy tolerance between observed usage (runtime) and billed usage (billing pipeline) must be < 0.5% monthly for enterprise accounts.
- Daily reconciliation report sent to account owners when monthly projection delta > 10%.

Telemetry retention and privacy:
- Default event retention: 90 days in high-cardinality store, 2 years aggregated in analytics store.
- All telemetry must omit prompt contents for customers with "suppress_prompt_telemetry" flag; store only token counts and hashes.

------------------------------------------------------------
Pricing & Packaging Implications

Fastpath is free for self-serve signups but toggles default monthly cap (fastpath cap = $500). For customers who exceed cap, flow options:
- Self-serve upgrade: expand monthly cap or purchase token bundle add-on.
- Contact sales: for Dedicated/Private capacity recommendation and custom pricing.

Pricing notes for product/finance teams:
- When Safety Net triggers fallback (fallback_variant used for > 50% of monthly tokens), bill at fallback variant unit price and flag account for fidelity migration review.
- If rate limiting applied, customers receive proportional credits for failed requests as part of the incident credit policy; crediting is computed as: credits_usd = min(monthly_cap_usd, estimated_loss_usd) rounded to nearest $1.

Suggested default price multipliers (for estimator UI):
- primary variant: base price multiplier = 1.0
- fallback_variant: multiplier = 0.4
- quantized runtime (q4): multiplier = 0.65

------------------------------------------------------------
Implementation Requirements (Checklist)

Table: key requirement | owner | acceptance criteria
- Project-level CSN config store | Platform Configs | persisted, immutable historical changes, audit log available
- Console quickstart UI | Console team | quickstart flows render in <3s and include cost estimator
- Runtime guardrail enforcement | Serving Runtime | enforcement end-to-end demonstrated in e2e test with synthetic burst
- Telemetry hooks | Runtime & Billing | events emitted with documented schema, ingestion tests green
- Billing reconciliation | Billing team | daily ingest/aggregation pipeline, <0.5% drift for sample tenant

Minimum acceptance tests (automated):
1. Preflight run returns cost estimate and does not enable production keys until user confirms.
2. Synthetic burst that triggers degradation step 1 logs csn.degrade.event and reduces token limit.
3. Hitting monthly cap triggers fallback_variant and billing-bridge ingests the fallthrough usage line items.

------------------------------------------------------------
Rollout Plan

Phase 1 (internal pilot) - 4 weeks:
- Enable Fastpath and CSN for Redwood internal orgs.
- Run synthetic loadtests and reconciliation smoke tests.
- Collect developer feedback via 3 SE interviews.

Phase 2 (beta customers) - 6 weeks:
- Invite 10 customers across startups and mid-market segments.
- Observe two billing cycles for reconciliation stability.
- Iterate on UI messaging and cap defaults.

Phase 3 (general availability):
- Gradual ramp: 10% of new signups get Fastpath by default, increment weekly.
- Monitor: monthly projection vs billed delta, cap trigger rates, CSN false positives.
- Post-GA: surface "fastpath adoption" metric on product dashboard.

Key roll owners:

- Console: Simone Alvarez
- Serving Runtime: Thomas Reed

------------------------------------------------------------
Operational Runbook (short)

When a customer hits projected spend > 75% of cap:
1. Console sends automated in-app notice and email (template id: CSN-75).
2. Alert page in SRE runbook auto-opens with timeline and last 60m token rate.
3. If escalation required, oncall SRE follows Incident checklist: verify telemetry, confirm fallback routing, coordinate with Account Exec.
4. After event, CSN post-incident: generate reconciliation summary and proposed cap adjustment.

Playbook for disputed invoices related to CSN actions:
1. Customer raises support ticket with billing tag.
2. Billing team pulls csn.usage.sample payload for disputed window.
3. If discrepancy > 1%, open tier-2 audit with runtime team and provide provisional credit.

------------------------------------------------------------
Release Notes (v1.0)

Release date: 2026-09-01
Highlights:
- Fastpath onboarding flow launched in Console (default profile + benchmark preflight).
- Consumption Safety Net implemented with 3-step graceful degradation and fallback routing.
- Telemetry schema csn.* v1 defined and integrated into billing-bridge ingestion.
- Default caps configured for self-serve tenants and upgrade paths added in Console billing page.

Known limitations & follow-ups:
- Per-route cap (fine-grained within a single project) is not supported in v1. Target for Q1 2027.
- Prompt-level telemetry suppressed for privacy flags is implemented at control plane but aggregated edge cases remain; follow-up to harden in Q4 2026.

Appendices

A: Console messaging templates (ids):
- CSN-75: "You're approaching your monthly consumption safety cap"
- CSN-100: "Your project has entered recovery mode: fidelity reduced"

B: Useful commands / dashboards:
- Console -> Projects -> <project> -> Consumption Insights (new tab)
- Internal dashboard: /dashboards/csn/project-summary (view-only)
- CLI preflight: redwood demo preflight --project <id>

C: Contacts and escalation:
- Product owner: nadia.park@redwood.ai
- Oncall SRE: see team rota in /oncall/rota
- Billing lead: arjun.patel@redwood.ai

D: Next roadmap items (priority order)
1. Per-route and session-level caps (Q1 2027)
2. Auto-upgrade recommendation engine in Console (Q2 2027)
3. Deeper fidelity metrics in console (token-level efficiency and hallucination signal) (Q3 2027)
